they merely give rise to all sorts of divergent views within their own minds. If one can truly 'sit and cut it off,' then even if a Buddha comes, thirty blows;
even if a Mara comes, thirty blows. A student asked, "If you say they must 'sit and cut it off,' why do you strike both when a Buddha comes and when a Mara comes?"
The Master said, "Precisely because they are called 'Buddha' and called 'demon,' I could not help but strike them.

When the Master arrived in Hangzhou, he heard that various masters and Dharma teachers, such as Gu Shi and Huiwen Shi, as well as lay officials who protect the Dharma, had each instructed their attendants to carry letters to welcome him.
In the letter from Dharma Teacher Huiwen, it said: "Today, the Great Assembly..."
"I wish to have a formal encounter with the Abbot. If the Abbot comes, I have already fallen into the realm of conceptual consciousness;

if the Abbot does not come, it would still be a lack of compassion. When the Master finished reading this, he immediately tore all the scrolls into pieces and, with a stern countenance and a harsh voice, said, "How dare these hirelings bring such a defeat upon me? The Master then entered and ascended the hall.
Huìyún stood up. "Preceptor, do not try to wield an axe at a carpentry door. The Master gave him a slap and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
Huìyún’s face turned red, and he remained speechless. The Master said, "You dead man! Hearing this, Master Wengu led the assembly in prostrating themselves.

The Master, together with Grand Master Daguan, Venerable Yuechuan, Grand Tutor Tao Shikui, Minister of the Imperial Household Zuoxinyuan, Secretariat Drafter Huang Shenxuan, Court Gentleman Zeng Zhongshui, and Zhu Youshi, was enjoying the moon at Jiaxi Temple.
Shenxuan asked about the karmic conditions regarding Mazu, Nanquan, and Baizhang’s viewing of the moon, requesting a word from the Master. The Master said:

"You lie down while I stand; you must not explain this to others. Be careful, Xuan, rise quickly, and apologize for your error. Both masters said, "The words I have spoken do not fall short of those of such a person."
Yuan Liuhui of the Ministry of Personnel asked, "What is the meaning behind Nanquan’s killing of the cat? The Master said, "Do not slander Zhaozhou.
Liuhui asked, "How is it slandering him? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!"
Xun Chao asked Suyunpu, "I have seen the embroidered mandarin ducks; you may look at them yourself. But the golden needle is not passed on to others.
"How is this golden needle? the Master said, "When I traveled through the capital, I never encountered a single person [who possessed it].
Suyunpu was about to offer further words when the Master said, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away."
A monk asked, "Is bowing correct? Is making inquiries correct? The Master said, "It follows your own delusions. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "What have you accomplished? The monk bowed.
Huangqiao Hai asked: "The Brahmin engaged in debate with the World-Honored One and then swept his sleeves and departed.
On the way, he attained realization and said to his disciples: 'In my doctrine, there are two points of defeat. If one accepts this view, the point of defeat is coarse;
if one does not accept this view, the point of defeat is subtle. What is the coarse point of defeat? What is the subtle point of defeat? "
The Master said, "Even I do not know. Huang was speechless.
Li Jiuyi, the Prefectural Governor, stepped forward and asked, "Why is it that not a single person among the assembly has raised a question? The Master replied, "They are all Buddhas.
Li asked, "What do you mean by that? The Master said, "To ask is already to fall into the second gate. A monk then asked, "Setting aside the gates..."
"Is there a separate place for 'acting for others' outside of the 'expedient means of wind'? The Master said, "I am not as good as everyone else.
[The monk] asked, "Why are you not as good as them? The Master said, "They lack expedient means."
The Jinshi (Metropolitan Graduate) Huang Shisi asked, "What is the 'knife that kills'? The Master said, "A cloth drum suspended in the courtyard—who would dare strike it?
He asked, "What is the 'sword that gives life'? The Master said, "Although you are a junior student, you are worthy of it.

He asked again, "In the teachings it is said: 'To repent' means to repent for one's prior faults; 'to regret' means to regret one's subsequent transgressions. But as for the actions committed in the interim, how should one deal with them?"

"How is it? the Master said, "It can only be known by oneself. Later, because the main gate of Fucheng Monastery had been destroyed by fire, someone asked, "Everyone says the diamond body is indestructible;
where have these four men gone? The Master said, "That which is destroyed is not the diamond [body].
[The questioner] said, "What about this one? The Master said, "The Tathāgata cannot be seen through physical form."
Haiyan asked, "When you entered the city, Master, how many skulls did you pierce? The Master replied, "Two or three.
Haiyan reached out his hand and said, "Bring them here for me to see. The Master said, "One who asks others for things is no true adept.

A monk asked, "In my daily life, throughout the six periods of the day and night, I do not recite the Buddha’s name, I do not practice Chan meditation, I do not study the teachings, and I do not sever delusions."
[The student] said, "I do not grasp at suchness; I simply eat when hungry and sleep when tired, acting according to my own nature with total freedom.
Is this in accord with the Way? The Master said, "That nature of perfect enlightenment is called 'sickness' precisely because it cannot be attained by mere compliance.
[The student] asked, "If that is so, then everything falls outside the four sicknesses. How, then, should one practice? The Master said, "All sentient beings have already realized [it]."
Yuánjué asked, "When sentient beings transform into insentient things, where does the Buddha-nature go? The Master said, "Sentient beings transform into insentient things.
Yuánjué said, "What about the Buddha-nature? The Master said, "Where would it go? Yuánjué said, "If sentient beings transform into sentient beings, for what reason [does this happen]?"
[The monk] said, "It is a transformation. The Master said, "Sentient beings transform sentient beings.
You ask about the Buddha-dharma; you do not ask anything else. [The monk] asked, "How will the Master return to the abbot’s quarters? The Master said, "I shall not return to the abbot’s quarters.
[The monk] asked, "Why do you not return? The Master said, "Because of the illness of sentient beings."
The Regional Inspector Shen Donghua asked, "How do you explain 'the source'? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, have never opened my mouth from the beginning.
Donghua said, "This very statement is the source. The Master said, "I do not know either."
Question: "When one first attains realization, are there guest and host? The Master said: "Guest and host are distinct. Question: "Is there still discrimination?
The Master said: "Two eyes facing two eyes."
A questioner asked, "Are the School of Nature (Xingzong) and the School of Characteristics (Xiangzong) the same or different? The Master said, "Turning the hand over and turning the hand back.

The questioner asked, "Is it pleasant when sleeping? Is it pleasant when lecturing on the sutras? The Master said, "Both are pleasant. The questioner asked, "Is this pleasure within or without? The Master said, "It is both within and without."
The Master said, "In times of adversity, one perfects oneself; in times of success, one brings universal benefit to the world.
[The Layman] said, "Do not apply our Confucian texts to this. The Master said, "I was speaking of ordinary matters; you, Layman, have made a book out of them."

A questioner asked about the most essential points within the School of Nature (Xingzong) and requested that the Master show him one or two. The Master said, "In the School of Nature, there are no such essential points.
The questioner asked, "Did you meet Zhou Haimen? The Master replied, "I have met him. The questioner asked, "Is he a follower of Daoxue or of the Chan school?"
The Master said, "This is the study of the Way. [The scholar] said, "If that is so, then it would not be appropriate. The Master said, "When it is Heaven, it is Heaven;
when it is man, it is man.
Zhang Hanlin of Jinyang asked, "At what time did the World-Honored One ascend the seat? The Master said, "I do not yet know, lay brother, what—"
When Master Chu heard that the World-Honored One had ascended the seat, the Layman [Zhao] was about to deliberate upon it. The Master said, "Chu does not even know this; when do you intend to ask?
The Master then engaged in a discourse with Wang Jinshi on the indestructible diamond body. A monk standing nearby remarked, "If one proclaims in such a manner..."
"The Buddha-Dharma has been swept away and exhausted. The Master said, "If it were a true lion, it certainly would not act like this.
[The monk] said, "But there are also jackals who would be willing to howl in such a manner. The Master said, "Precisely! Precisely! [The monk] said, "It is well to accept this responsibility.
The Master said, "You accept it; I accept it. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the monk hesitated, the Master shouted and sent him out.
Question: His feet do not tread upon the branches, yet his mouth holds a tree branch. When someone below asks, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
if one answers him, one cannot avoid losing one's body and life. I wonder, Master, what skillful means do you have to convey this message?
The Master said: "I am certainly one who has no life."
Yangjuemalachi asked, citing the Buddha’s words: "I have not killed a living being for immeasurable kalpas; why then was this girl born?
The Master said, "When did she ever come forth from below? He replied, "If that is so, then while she was in the womb, there was nothing that could be done.
The Master said, "Once she has been born, it is no longer like that."
One day the Master sighed and said, "Living in this world is like dipping one's hand into boiling water; it is better to return home. A monk asked, "Where would you go?
The Master replied, "Only those who truly understand are my fellow practitioners."
A monk asked, "Are the Zen of the Patriarchs and the Zen of the Tathāgata the same or different? The Master said, "Guo is Hangzhou.
The monk said, "If that is so, then they are the same. The Master said, "The Yangtze River divides this and that."
A monk asked, "After this body has perished, where will one find a place to establish oneself and sustain one's life?
The Master said, "To ask such a great matter, you must first prostrate three times; I will not speak for you. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Stop, stop! Where will you establish yourself?
The monk hesitated. The Master rebuked him. The monk knelt again and begged for instruction. The Master said, "Go! Even a Buddha cannot do anything about it."
"What is it that you do not obtain?
A monk asked, "Is it permitted for those outside the gate to enter? The Master said, "When have you ever been inside the gate? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Good words are never exhausted by questioning.
A monk asked, "How can one see one's original face? The Master said, "You are a man without a face.
The monk said, "Why should I alone be without a face? The Master said, "If you had a face, why would you seek to see it?"
The Head of the Kitchen asked, "The dust fills the sky; when will it become pure? The Master said, "For now, just keep the fire burning.

Baopu came to pay his respects. Upon rising from his prostrations, he asked, "There are many people here; I do not know how many lions there are among them. The Master said, "Every person is a Buddha.
Baopu was about to offer further words, but the Master shook his hand to stop him.
Nanming requested to serve as an attendant who does not handle administrative affairs. The Master said, "In this old monk’s place, there is not even enough room for the point of a锥 (a small awl).
Nanming was about to offer a response, but the Master shook his hand to stop him.
The Master was attending to the monk Zhinan. The Master called to him, "Zhinan, my four elements are in disharmony;
can you cure me? Zhinan replied, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master then called to Molang, "Can you cure me? Molang said, "Why such idle chatter?
The Master remarked, "It is better than this illiterate one."
Xueting entered for an interview. Rising to prostrate, he asked, "What are you doing here, Preceptor? The Master said, "I am killing people. Xue said, "Do you possess such a capability?
The Master said, "It has been five or six years since we last met; I thought your nostrils had turned upward."
"Originally, you were still acting with such reservations. Go out.
[The Master] asked, "What is meant by 'I have nothing hidden from you'? The teacher lifted his foot and said, "Look at how many lines there are on the sole of my foot."

Question: "What is it that 'the myriad dharmas return to the One,' and where does the One return? The Master held up a silk cord and said, "This was bought for six-tenths of a silver ingot in Hangzhou."
While the Master was engaged in conversation with a layperson, a certain layman asked, "How can you, Reverend, speak in such a manner? The Master replied, "He does not want the Buddha-dharma.
When the man asked, "What if he did want it? the Master thrust his hand into the lapel of his robe and made a gesture, saying, "It would be finished just like this."

Following the discourse on the Master’s hand wheeling the prayer beads, a question was asked: "When the Master wheels the prayer beads with his hands while speaking to others with his mouth, is this reciting the Buddha's name, or is it merely talking?
The Master picked up the prayer beads and said: "If there were a knife in my hand, you would say that I am committing murder."
The lay practitioner Zhang Hongso of Yiyang asked, "What is it to let one move pass? The Master said, "For now, please have some cake.
[Zhang] said, "It is still right here. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, have never been like that from the start.
[Zhang] said, "If that is so, then you surpass your own teacher. The Master said, "Lay practitioner, do not defame others."
A monk asked, "The tiger gives birth to seven cubs; which one has no tail? The Master said, "This very one has no tail. The monk requested a verse, and the Master composed this:
In question and answer there is no difference at all; It is like using a fan to cover [one's face]. When people come, they must meet me face-to-face; Do not look for flowers within the fan.
A monk asked, "What is 'one who is old'? The Master said, "The person of the past still remains; it is not that the person of the past has ceased to be.
It is simply that children do not see clearly. The monk asked, "What is 'one who is not old'? The Master said, "Set aside this illusory body and see the ultimate reality.
Who then can be called a white-haired old man? The monk asked, "What is 'that which a close person cannot cross over'? The Master said, "The arising of a single thought."

"Obstructed. Question: "What is it that he does not cross over for his own kin? The Master said: "When the whole body is cast down, who is there to be considered kin? Question: "What is it that does not borrow anything from another person's house?

The Master said: "To have words still constitutes delusion; to be wordless is not yet the truth. If you attempt to seek the profound principle, it is nothing but dust in your eyes. He then spoke a verse in response to all these questions: When the whole body is cast down, who is there to be considered kin?

To have words still constitutes delusion; to be wordless is not yet the truth. If you attempt to seek the profound principle, it is nothing but dust in your eyes. If you wish to know the meaning of this, look directly at the face before you.
It is said: "On this day last year, I saw lotus flowers; on this day this year, human affairs have changed.
All this is but the clever schemes born of one's own mind, wishing to divide two people when there is not a single tongue [to do so]."

The Master cited the karmic conditions concerning Jiufeng’s examination of the Head Seat and questioned a monk: "Setting aside for a moment the instructions to 'rest' and 'cease,' what is it like to go forth as a single white silk ribbon?
The monk said, "The mendicant’s staff hangs from an ox’s head; the *kāṣāya* wraps around a dog’s bone. The Master said, "Not so.
If he had asked me, I would have called out to him, ‘Prostrate yourself! And when he rose from his prostration, I would have said to him:"
"You have served as my attendant," said Master [Zhaozhou].
Layman Liu Yantian recounted the karmic conditions regarding Zhang Tianjue’s verse on the "Original Cause. The Master asked, "What is the 'original cause' of the verse?
The layman repeated the verse once more. The Master immediately let out a shout and said, "Can it be called the 'original cause' of the verse?"
The questioner asked, "Does the Master wish to become a bodhisattva? The Master said, "I do not. The questioner pressed, "Why do you not?
The Master replied, "If you want my head, eyes, marrow, and brain, what will I have left to give you?"
Regarding the case of Layman Luting: "Zishao [said] 'the pattern of things' (*wugé*), while Miaoxi [said] 'things patterned' (*wùgé*). What was their intended meaning?

Luting said, "The boundless seas of lands do not separate self and other by even a hair’s breadth. The Master said, "This is merely literary phrasing; you have not yet grasped the ancients' true intent.
A bystander asked, "Is 'overcoming the self and returning to ritual' (*kǐjǐ fùlǐ*) the 'patterning of things'? The Master shook his head.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the kalpa-fire blows across the ocean floor and the mountain drums strike one another with the wind?
The monk overturned the meditation seat, and the Master laughed heartily.
The monk then asked, "The joy of the road is ultimately not arriving home; what is the joy of the road? The Master said, "Open."
The mouth forms a pair of stakes; raising the eyebrows, two or three fall away. "What is the matter of arriving home? The Master said, "If you want the head, cut it off and take it.
Question: "The great chiliocosm is a bubble in the ocean. Apart from the water, what is the bubble? The Master said, "What is [the water]?"
"You are separated from the water.
Next, regarding the master’s counting of his rosary beads, a monk asked, "Why does the Master not let them go loose, but instead keeps them squeezed together?

The master replied, "One uses a crutch while riding a horse. The monk asked, "What is 'carrying along the common path'? The master held up his rosary beads to show him. The monk asked again... [text fragment ends]

[The monk] asked, "What is 'the subtle embrace that penetrates the source'? The Master also raised his rosary. [The monk] asked, "Is this 'carrying along' the same as or different from 'the subtle embrace'?

The Master also raised his rosary. [The monk] asked, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "If it were, I would cut it off and take it away. [The monk] asked, "What is the perfect circle (*yuánxiàng*)?
The Master said, "A large sesame cake. [The monk] asked, "What is the dark mechanism (*ànjī*)? The Master said, "Ascending the clouds."
Feng asked, "What is the ocean of meaning? The Master said, "A pavilion halfway up a mountain. He asked, "Are the ocean of words and the ocean of meaning the same or different?
The Master said, "If they were different, there would be two; if they are not different, they are a pair. He asked, "What is intentional speech? The Master said:
A mute person casting a spell on another. [The student] asked, "What is 'discussing in silence'? The Master said, "Wenbo meeting Confucius. [The student] asked, "What is 'reciprocal yielding'?
The Master said, "A filial son avoids mentioning his father's name."
While the Master was enjoying the cool breeze, he sighed and said, "Nowadays, the Zen of the Patriarchs has been thrown into confusion by various quarters.
I shall now speak only of the Tathāgata-dhyāna. A monk asked, "Are the Patriarchs' Zen and the Tathāgata's Zen the same or different? The Master said, "A single drop of ink.
The monk pressed further, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "In both places, dragons are formed."

Question: "Dechen (Guṇamegha) constantly dwells atop Mount Sublime Peak (Sudharmakūṭa), yet Sudhana visits him like a river flowing past without seeing him. The Master said: "Facing one another, we do not recognize each other. The questioner asked:
"How is it that he is seen again on a different peak? The Master said: "As soon as you raise your intention, you know he is there."
Question: "What is the summit of Tongxuan Peak? It is not of this human world; there is no dharma outside the mind—before one's eyes are the green mountains.
The Master said: "If you want me to speak of it, I shall be filled with shame. The questioner said: "I do not understand. I beg the Master to descend to the common level [to explain].
The Master said: "Do not seek understanding through sounds and forms."
A monk asked, "Sentient beings and insentient things share one body. What is this one body? The Master said, "Close your throat, lips, and mouth;
then tell me, bring forth the insentient for me to see."
A monk asked, "What is it like to hold a hoe with empty hands? The Master said, "I have a mouth, but I cannot speak.
The monk asked, "What is the principle of not being born or dying amidst birth and death? The Master said, "My tongue is three inches too short."
A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter? The Master said, "Wearing clothes and eating food.
Another monk asked, "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master assumed a stern expression and raised his voice, enumerating the monk's past transgressions.
The monk, feigning anger, took his leave. The Master said, "You asked how it is when the mirror has not yet been polished; go ahead and polish this one spot! The monk remained standing there.
A monk asked, "If one clearly knows that birth and death are the dharma of non-arising, why is it that one is nonetheless carried away by birth and death?
The Master said, "It is simply this rosary. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Not understanding is actually good."
The Monk Raises the Case. Heling Su was once asked by a monk who knocked on his door. Su asked, "Who is it? The monk replied, "It is a monk. Su said, "Not only a monk;
even if it were the Buddha himself, he would not be admitted. The monk then asked, "Master, why would he not be admitted? The Master said, "He was deceived right before his eyes.
He added, "If I had been there at that time, I would have simply said, 'Thank you for your compassion, Master.'"
A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "A single bright moon shines upon Gusu.
Another monk asked, "An ancient said, 'If I were to exclusively expound the Dharma of the Lineage (Zongcheng), the grass before the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep.'"
"How do you, Master, instruct people? The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "What are you saying? A monk standing nearby repeated his previous question.
The Master said, "If I were to constantly exalt the Dharma-gate of our school, the weeds before the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep."
A monk asked, "There is the one path to nirvana; I beg you to point out its beginning. The Master said, "Which is the Peak Beloved by the Emperor?
Another monk asked, "'The self-mind grasps the self-mind, and what is not illusion becomes an illusory dharma. By not grasping, there is nothing that is not non-illusion.
What is 'not grasping, there is nothing that is not non-illusion'? The Master did not answer. Instead, he spoke with a bystander and then asked the monk, "Was it you who asked just now?"
"What is it? The monk repeated his previous question. The Master said, "You lack quick wit.

The monk asked, "When the myriad dharmas return to the One, where does the One return? The monk had become somewhat more proficient, yet he was still unable to attain a state of vast, unimpeded freedom.
He asked, "I do not know how to proceed further; please instruct me. The Master said, "Zhaozhou said, 'In Qingzhou, I made a robe of cotton cloth.'"
"It weighs seven *jin*. How do you understand this? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, you must strive to understand it.
The Master went to the middle hall to visit Master Wunian and asked, "An ancient said, 'It is like a single flake of snow flying onto a red-hot furnace.
Tell me, did that ancient truly possess the eye to penetrate the barrier? Wunian said, "I do not see anything at all."
"O ancient one! The Master hurriedly pointed and said, "Behind you? The monk thought, "I must stop.
A monk asked, "When Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī discussed the Dharma-gate of non-duality, was it silence? Or was it not silence?
If it were silence, then Mañjuśrī’s words would be superfluous; if it were not silence, then Vimalakīrti’s effort would have been in vain."
[The monk] asked: "What is the meaning? The Master said: "He would not even suffice to be your slave. The monk said:
"I have already attained the 'unbreakable head' of Buddha-recitation. The Master said: "Release it! [The monk] stepped forward and asked:
"How do I release it? The Master said: "Release it again! The monk again sought a skillful means. The Master lifted up his skirt and said: "The egg is here!"
A monk asked, "The fundamental nature is pure and serene; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The Master said, "It is this very sound of your question.
[The monk] asked, "I request the Master to explain the meaning of 'all dharmas are like illusions. The Master said, "An explanation would not suffice."
The Master entered the hall to examine the assembly. One monk made two circles with his fingers and placed them over his eyes;
the Master shook his head and said, "Not so. Another monk snapped his fingers; the Master shook his head and said, "Not so. A third monk stepped forward without opening his mouth;
the Master shook his head and said, "Not so. A fourth monk approached him; the Master shook his head and said, "Not so, not so. The monk then prostrated himself.
He prostrated and rose. The Master said, "What was it that I was saying to you when you immediately prostrated? At that moment, a sick monk threw down his meditation cushion.
The Master assumed an expression of alarm and said, "The entire assembly is not equal to this sick monk."
There was a blind man who requested instruction. The Master took him by the hand and pointed, saying, "This is a chair; this is a table.
The blind man immediately prostrated himself. The Master said, "The entire assembly is not equal to this blind man."
At one time, eight people were struck by lightning. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the eight people being struck by lightning? The Master said, "A great function.
The monk pressed further, "When heaven does not cover and earth does not support them, what sin have they committed? The Master said, "The great earth is dark and silent."
A monk asked, "What is it like before one's parents were born? The Master looked at a nearby monk and said, "He has already awakened.
The monk pressed further, "Ultimately, what is it like before one's parents were born? The Master said, "Soliciting alms.
The monk asked, "After soliciting alms, what then? The Master said, "Offering fruit."
A monk asked, “What is the matter that transcends [the world]? The Master said, “The golden wind is revealed in its essence. The monk pressed, “What is the matter that descends [into the world]?
The Master said, “Before the donkey, behind the horse. The monk pressed, “What is ‘before the donkey, behind the horse’?

The Master said, “When a servant sees a maidservant, he is full of courtesy. The monk pressed, “What is ‘when a servant sees a maidservant, he is full of courtesy’? The Master said, “Dragging through mud and carrying water. The monk pressed on.
[The student] asked, "What is 'dragging through mud and carrying water'? The Master said, "Seven hands and eight feet. [The student] further asked, "What about seven hands and eight feet?
The Master said, "Thirty painful blows of the staff."
The Master entered the city and saw a blind monk sitting upright by the side of the street.
The Master prostrated himself before the monk dozens of times and then patted his back, saying, "Do not forget. The monk joined his palms and said, "Amitābha Buddha.
At that time, the crowd in the marketplace gathered around and asked, "Who is this person? The Master replied, "This is an ancient buddha."
Tao Shi Kui left behind a rhinoceros-horn belt for his teacher. A worldly man attempted to deceive him, asking, "The Master is a Bodhisattva of great cultivation;
you ought to receive my prostrations. The Master said, "I am not a Bodhisattva of cultivation; there is no need for prostrations.
The man pressed further, saying, "Is it not the case that the Master is a Bodhisattva of cultivation? The Master replied, "If I were a Bodhisattva of cultivation..."
"Sa. "All you Māras have come to cut off my flesh. The gentlemen all departed with expressions of shame.
A householder asked, "Before one's parents were born, please, Master, speak a single word. The Master said, "One cannot rely entirely on this old monk.
He asked again, "What is 'directly seeing one's nature'? The Master said, "This question is no small matter. [The householder] said, "It is no small matter."
"What is it? The Master said, "If you ask me, you will not get it.
Mai Lang asked, "What is the meaning of Sudhana’s pilgrimage everywhere? [The Master replied,] "The black bean has not yet sprouted.
The Master said, "I do not answer. [Mai Lang] asked, "Why do you not answer? The Master said, "If I answered, the sprout would grow."
A monk asked, "What is the wondrous nature that is perfectly luminous and free from all names and appearances? The Master held up his staff and said, "What do you call this?
The monk replied, "A staff. The Master said, "Then how can you say it is free from all names and appearances?"
A monk asked, "At a place where wisdom does not reach, what is the essence? The Master said, "Above all, do not speak of it.
The monk said, "Beating the mallet and raising the whisk—these words and phrases are all wisdom. What, then, is the place where it does not reach? The Master said, "Whose words are these?
I do not remember them; try reciting them for me. The monk said, "This is wisdom. What, then, is the place where it does not reach?"
The Master said, "You lack quick-wittedness. Why did you not examine his background? After a long silence, he said, "What else do you wish to ask?
As the monk prepared to speak further, the Master pushed him away and entered the room.
A monk asked, "Since he is a lion cub, why is it that he is bitten by a fox? The Master said, "I am so struck by your question that my mouth is completely stuffed.
The monk asked, "Why is this so? The Master said, "If one were truly a lion, one would certainly never chase after a clod of earth."
While Master Baolin was lecturing on the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, the Master happened to enter the temple. The assembly requested that he lecture on the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*.
The Master said, "You have already lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra*; why do you want me to lecture on the *Diamond Sūtra*?

Although the assembly requested it repeatedly, the Master said, "You all get out! and then performed a somersault. The assembly laughed loudly and asked, "Master, you are quite old and venerable; how [can you do this]?"
"What is this 'performing a somersault'? The Master said, "I simply want you all to smile once.
Minghe asked, "From antiquity to the present, I believe there has never been a second person [like me]. Why then can I not penetrate this kōan?
The Master said, "What kōan is there that you cannot penetrate? Bring it forward and let us see. As Minghe was about to open his mouth, [the Master struck him].
The Master said, "Go, go! You are no good person.
After the layman Zhou Huading asked, "After we part today, where shall we meet? the Master replied, "Be careful on the road."
A monk asked, "Frequently calling for 'Little Jade' was originally for no reason; it was simply to have the husband recognize the voice.
"What is the voice? The Master said, "This is not the voice."
A monk asked, "What is it like when one does not fall into birth and extinction? The Master said, "I do not answer. The monk said, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "Expedient means itself is birth and extinction."
The Master asked the assembly, "What was the meaning behind Nanquan’s act of beheading the cat? One monk called out his own name; another monk pushed his meditation cushion down to the floor;
another said, "These two have already spoken; what can I say? The Master said, "A great pity. Xu asked, "In what way?
The Master said, "With a single word, he reached Xuzhou."
A monk asked, "When Master Ma’s single shout left Baizhang deaf for three days, did it manifest his great capacity (*dajī*) or did it manifest his great function (*dàyòng*)?
The Master said, "It is the same rice and flour. The monk asked, "What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "It depends on how people process them."
A monk asked, "I am contemplating the 'Mu' (無) word-phrase, yet I have not attained a point of entry. I beg the Master for a skillful means.
The Master said, "It is rare indeed to find one who does not attain a point of entry."
A monk asked, "Yesterday while bathing, I attained a certain realization, yet I am simply unable to express it.
The Master pointed to a young attendant and said, "Does he know it as well? The monk replied, "He knows it too.
The Master said, "If one truly knows it, one will certainly not be turned by others."
A monk asked, "In the state where there is no dreaming and no conceptualization, who is my master? The Master said, "What is your name?
The monk said, "Dahua. The Master said, "Go for now."
A monk asked, "Master Mokṣa said, 'If you can speak, you die under the cangue; if you cannot speak, you die under the cangue.
If one had asked you, Master, what would you have said? The Master replied, "This wild fox spirit!
He added, "I am certainly one who has no life or destiny."

A monk asked, "To study by transcending mind, intellect, and consciousness, and cutting off the path of ordinary beings and sages—how, for instance, does one transcend mind, intellect, and consciousness?
The Master said, "Bring me your mind, intellect, and consciousness, and I will separate them from you for you. The monk said, "They cannot be brought forth.
The Master said, "Since they cannot be brought forth, what is there to be separated?"
A monk asked, "When there is no dreaming and no thinking, where is the host? The Master said, "Right now, where is the host?
The monk hesitated. The Master shouted. The monk bowed. The Master said, "This shout was originally meant for you to let out."
A monk asked, "What is that which transcends and does not borrow? The Master said, "I do not hear clearly;
ask again. The monk said, "I am unwilling to ask. The Master said, "This is borrowing. The monk shouted. The Master said, "Still borrowing.
The monk shouted again. The Master said, "Still borrowing. The monk said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said, "After a hundred shouts, what then?"
[The Master] rose. The monks prostrated, saying, "He has dispersed the assembly. He then returned to the midst of the community. The Master said, "Such is the extent of his skill.
The Head Seat asked, "Please, Reverend, speak those words that have not yet been uttered. The Master said, "I would rather incur the national taboo than fail to speak."
Tongue.
A monk asked, "What is the great function? The Master said, "To strike down ten million people without being called a man of rash temperament.
Mayang asked, "What is the root of non-abiding? The Master raised his whisk. Mayang said, "Does non-abiding still exist?"
"Is there a fundamental basis? The Master asked. Mazu replied, "What was it you just asked? Mazu said, "The basis of non-abiding.
The Master asked, "Is there still a basis? Mazu bowed.
Mai Lang asked, "What is meant by 'the three realms are mind-only' and 'all phenomena are consciousness-only'? The Master said, "How old are you?
Mai replied, "I was born in the same lineage as the Master, though we shall not die in the same lineage. The Master said, "The three realms are mind-only;
all phenomena are consciousness-only."
The student Xiucai asked, "In my mind, Master, there is as it were a certain principle, yet I simply cannot put it into words.
The Master said, "Is it that you cannot put it into words? He replied, "I cannot put it into words. The Master said, "Then you are deceiving me; my ears are deaf!"
A monk asked, "When the four great elements have fallen away, what else remains? The Master said, "I cannot hear clearly; try asking again.
As the monk was about to speak again, the Master said, "Is that not it?"
Bao Xingquan asked, "What is the phrase for escaping birth and death? The Master said, "Two eyes facing two eyes.
He asked, "After two eyes face two eyes, what then? The Master said, "You do not speak; I do not ask. He asked, "If you neither speak nor ask, how can one escape birth and death?
The Master said, "At this very moment, bring forth birth and death and I will give it to you."
Fanglang asked, "How can one listen to the Dharma without using a conditioned mind and yet attain the nature of phenomena?
The Master said, "Each and every thing flows forth from within your own breast; only then does it cover heaven and earth. Fanglang asked, "What is this 'own'?"
A verse flowing from the breast. The Master said: "The stone woman is practiced at playing, yet she has no needle or thread; the wooden puppet can ladle soup, yet it never wets the broth.
A monk asked: "I clearly understand this one point, yet I am unable to take it up. Where does the sickness lie? The Master said:
"One who intends to seek the profound essence is like a blind man encountering a tree.
A monk asked, "The Great Master Da once questioned the abbot of the Two Temples: 'The entire earth is the Buddha-body; tell me, where is the Buddha-body?
The abbot was speechless. What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "He was simply knocked over by the abbot."
[The monk] asked, "Why did the Great Master strike the abbot? The Master said, "This was a blow given to one who has already been wronged. [The monk] asked, "What do you mean by that?
The Master said, "It should have been the Great Master himself who ate it."
The Master was observing by the water’s edge. Wolang asked, "When devas and humans see this, they see it as lapis lazuli; when fish and dragons see it, they regard it as their home.
What do you, Preceptor, see? The Master said, "Water. Wolang said, "In that case, you have fallen into the realm of human perception. The Master said, "How clever!"
A monk asked, "It is said that realization through conditions is swift in its correspondence. Yet the ancients said, 'That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure.
How, then, does one attain such correspondence? The Master said, "Have you not heard that for that which enters through the gate, there is never any loss?

The monk asked, "To settle within the essence results in a slow gain of power. If one settles therein, why would one not gain power? The Master said, "At the very moment you attempt to seek it through thought, it turns away."
Yao’o asked, “A thought flickers up, yet it has no place of origin from the beginning. Since it has no place of origin, where does it flicker up?
The Master said, “You cannot ask this, and I cannot answer this. Yao’o asked, “My teacher spoke of the ‘inconceivable for a moment.
If it is inconceivable, with what could he speak of it even for a moment? The Master said, “Precisely because it is inconceivable. Yao’o asked, “Nanquan said...”
"Returning home is naturally the business of one's descendants. Dahui said, "In the end, he lets him have his way; how is this?
The Master said, "Out of affection for one's child, one does not notice their ugliness. He asked, "Are Nanquan and Dahui the same or different?
The Master said, "A single staff carried by two people."
Question: Why do the Buddhas of the three periods of time not know that they exist? The Master said: "Because they are too noble. Question:
Why, then, do the *lilu* (the cat) and the *baigu* (the white ox) know that they exist? The Master said: "Because they are too poor and lowly."
A monk asked, "I beg the Master to point out the essential heart-mind and the true meaning of liberation from birth and death.
The Master said, "From the beginning, I have never given a single word to anyone. The monk bowed in prostration.
A monk asked, "What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena? The Master held up one finger.
The monk said, "This is an object. The Master replied, "It has been obscured by clouds once again."
A monk asked, "If the cause is correct and the result is correct, why did Devadatta experience the bliss of the Third Dhyāna Heaven while in hell?
The Master said, "This does not belong to cause and effect. The monk requested a verse. The Master said, "This does not belong to cause and effect.
Sitting amidst boiling cauldrons and glowing coals, he stubbornly claims that no suffering reaches him. When has the Buddha-eye ever recognized him?"
Cao Yuan and Lingxu came from Jinsu. The Master asked them, "In the past, when the three Buddhas took their leave of the Fifth Patriarch, the Patriarch said, 'Go now;
later you will suffer a bout of fever, and only then will you remember me.

Later, they indeed fell ill and realized for themselves that what they had previously practiced was ineffective, so they returned to the Patriarch’s mountain. During your illness, what was it like? Yuan replied, "I..."
"It is simply illness. What can be done? The Master said, "I am not like that. Yuan said, "How about you, Master?
The Master said, "I simply look at the one who is not ill. Yuan said, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket.
The Master said, "If you want medicine, I will give you a prescription of rhubarb. Yuan said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said, "Castor beans are the best."
A monk asked, "I, your disciple, have come from afar to seek the Way and request the Master’s instruction. The Master said, "Without leaving this very place, it is ever serene;
if you seek it, you will find that it cannot be found. The monk said, "Seeing others visit the Way, I too have come to study it.
The Master said, "It is not well to follow after the footsteps of others. The monk bowed in prostration.

The Layman Feng asked, "In the Southern School, is the sound of the bell with form or without form? Mazu replied, "When the east wind blows, it sounds in the east; when the west wind blows, it sounds in the west.
The Layman then asked the Master, "Is the sound of the bell with form or without form?

The Master said, "The bell has already rung, and the wind has already passed. What need is there to speak of 'with form' or 'without form'? The Layman pressed further, "While the bell is ringing and the wind is blowing..."
"How is it at the time of birth? The Master said, "It is merely a waste of effort to lean your ear.

The monk Yuanming from Yunnan asked, "When the Great Matter is not yet clarified, it is as if one has lost one's parents; when the Great Matter is already clarified, it is as if one has lost one's parents—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "In neither case does it depend on another. [He] asked about the Prince Nalaka’s dismembering of his own bones...
He returned the flesh to his father and the bones to his mother; thereafter, he manifested his body in the void and preached the Dharma for his parents.
What is this original self of Nanda? The Master said: "Cease identifying with this skin-bag born of your mother. He asked: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth..."

"The trichiliocosm of sand-grains may all be destroyed; I do not know whether this [reality] is destroyed or not. Setting aside for now the question of destruction, what is the principle of non-destruction?
The Master said, "The four great elements. Question: "A white heron descends to the field—a thousand points of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of gold.
What kind of scene is this? The Master said, "Do not take it as an object. Question: "The object arises from the subject that perceives the object. The Master said, "Object..."
When the capacity to pursue [objects] subsides and both the capacity and the objects are forgotten, what is this thing? The Master said, "It cannot be called mind. Question:
"If one can transform objects, one is identical to the Tathāgata. But tell me, how does one transform Mount Sumeru? The Master said, "It cannot be called Mount Sumeru. Question:
"To interpret the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three periods. To deviate from a single word of the scriptures is to be the same as..."
Māra said, "What is this sutra? The Master replied, "'Thus have I heard. [The interlocutor] asked about the Sixth Patriarch’s words regarding the "bright mirror not being a stand.
[He had already] penetrated this barrier long ago, yet he concealed it back at the third watch so that no one would see him;

this must certainly involve a matter of formal transmission and reception, rather than merely explaining a sutra. Students may understand this through silent intuition. But tell me, what was it that was transmitted? The Master replied, "Zhi (之)."
At the place where they met, he did not permit outsiders to know of it.
The Master asked, "Shi Yu, what is the phrase that cannot be exhausted by a single utterance?
Yu replied, "To pay respects to the Master morning and evening is also but an ordinary matter."
He asked again, "As for the meaning of Zhaozhou’s 'No'—what is it? Yu said, "The Master enjoys playing chess; I know it somewhat.
The Master said, "What would you say if I asked about 'Yes'? Yu then offered this verse: "Every household has a cloth to cover their shame;
If one lets it down, it can serve as rain and dew. I only wonder at the old Zhaozhou of yore, Who cast away his headscarf."
He tucked up his trousers. The Master asked him again about the three "shoulds. He presented this verse: "Buddha-nature, no Buddha-nature;
The scale-weight fell into the water and never floated. If you can grasp the essential meaning of Zhaozhou, Clapping hands all day long, you will sing the *zhègū*."
Hanyue asked: "When Xinghua was the head seat under Sansheng, he once said:

'I have traveled throughout the south on my pilgrimage, yet I have never, even with the tip of my staff, encountered a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma. Sansheng asked: 'What kind of eyes do you possess to speak like that?
Xinghua then gave a shout. Sansheng said: 'It must be you who can do this. Later, [Xinghua] arrived at Dajue."
Jue asked, "I have heard you say that during your journey southward on pilgrimage, you never once encountered a person who had grasped the Buddha-dharma with the tip of your staff.
On what basis do you speak in such a manner? Huaihai then gave a shout.

As soon as he realized this, Huairang struck him. Huaihua shouted again. Huairang struck him once more. When they met the next day, Huairang said, "Yesterday I was suspicious of those two shouts of yours.
Huaihua shouted again. Huairang struck him again. Huaihua shouted once more. Huairang struck him yet again.
Huaihua said, "I learned a 'host and guest' phrase from my elder brother, Master Sansheng, but I have been completely defeated by you, elder brother. I wish to—"
"Such-and-such a person has found a dharma-gate of peace and happiness. Jue said, "You blind fellow! You have come here to meet with defeat.
He stripped off his patched robe and gave him a severe beating. Through this, Huihua was able to realize, beneath the words, the principle of how the late Master Linji received blows from Huangbo.
He then asked, "May I ask what is the principle behind those three times of being severely beaten? The Master said, "Contact."
Attached to things, they do not know their own suffering. When Xuefeng saw a monk approaching, he placed both hands on the gate, leaned his body out, and asked, "What is it?
The monk replied, "What is it? Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to his hut. After the monk spent the summer retreat at Yantou, he questioned Yantou about this.
Tou said, “Xuefeng and I were born from the same branch, but we die on different branches. If you wish to know the final word, it is simply this.
[The monk] asked, “What is the distinction between being born and dying together, and being born together but not dying together? The Master said, “Hú Zhāngsān; Hēi Lìsì.

A monk asked, "In the *Lotus Sūtra*, it says that the light shines universally upon as many lands as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.

Why then does the light from the white tuft between the eyebrows illuminate only eighteen thousand lands in the eastern direction? The Master said, "If you present one corner and do not have the other three corners follow, how can the whole be understood?"
Question: "Does the Buddha Candrasūryapradīpa return to the Dark Abyss Hell? The Master said: "He enters. Question:
"It is said that 'the Dharma is eternally without nature' and 'the seeds of Buddhahood arise from conditions. Since it is eternal, why do you also say it is 'without'?
Since there is no nature, why do you say it 'arises from conditions'? The Master said: "To open one's mouth is to create a pair of pegs."
Question: "There is but one gate, yet it is narrow and small. Where is this gate located? The Master said: "In heaven there are not two suns;
among men there are not two minds. Question:
"The treasury of the Lotus Sūtra is deep, firm, profound, and remote; no one can reach it. What is the treasury of the Lotus Sūtra?"
The Master said: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive.
Regarding the question of how the Stūpa of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna can accommodate two Tathāgatas, the Master said: "As soon as one opens the mouth, it is already too much."

Question: Regarding the manifestation of the Buddha’s stūpa, why must the transformation bodies gather back together? The Master said: "Only when one is completely free from all subtle attachments does one arrive at the state of not-knowing.
Question: When the Buddhas exchange greetings, why do they send only their attendants? The Master said: "One must also have a bystander cast a glance."

Question: Regarding the manifestation at the Dragon Palace, what was the underlying intent behind designating her specifically as a "girl"? The Master said: "It is because of such idle matters that ignorance grows. Question:
What kind of capacity did the Dragon Girl possess that she was able to offer the pearl so immediately? The Master said: "Where did you hear news of her?"
Question: "It is said that one sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him.

How do you understand the meaning of the ancients' distinction between 'reciprocal interplay' (huí-hù) and 'non-reciprocal interplay' (bù huí-hù)? The Master said: "If you wish to understand it, you will only go further away."
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the *śamatha*, *samādhi*, and *dhyāna* of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. What is 'wondrous'? The Master said, "Not wondrous.
[The monk] raised his golden-colored arm and asked, "Among these three contemplations (*trivipaśyanā*), which one does this arm subsume? The Master said, "It follows."
"Things give rise to the mind.

A questioner asked: "The *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* states that Vimalakīrti left behind only a single bed, lying upon it while suffering from illness. I do not know what kind of ailment this was. The Master said:
"To raise the mind is to be separated by a thousand li."
Question: "Do Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra still fall under the influence of karmic habitual tendencies? The Master said: "They do. Question:
"The *Vajracchedikā* says that if one sees all marks as non-marks, one then sees the Tathāgata.
I wonder, are these 'marks' and 'non-marks' the same or different? The Master said: "They are."
Question: "Can a dry excrement-stick still fit within the Sea of Fragrant Water? The Master said: "It is rather a world within a mote of dust. Question:
"When Vimalakīrti remained silent, at that very moment, where was the attendant? The Master said: "He followed [him]."
[The student] approaches.
He asks, "What is the guest phrase under the Caodong school? The Master says, "Having traversed a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks.
He asks, "What is the host phrase? The Master says, "Sitting alone within the alchemical crucible, without a companion."
Question: The *Awakening of Faith* says: "It does not rely on form or color; it does not rely on breath; it does not rely on space;

"Three monkeys playing with a winnowing fan."
A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter of a student? The Master said, "All four seasons have their moons; when autumn comes, it is exceptionally bright.
The monk asked, "After the old woman burned the hermitage, what did she realize after three years? The Master said, "The pure breeze."
He crossed the bamboo grove and asked, "Three times three before and three times three after. He inquired, "Master, how many do you reckon? The Master replied, "The calf is three feet long."
Question: "The mud ox at the bottom of the sea runs off with the moon; the stone tiger before the cliff sleeps while cradling its cub.

I wonder which one it is? The Master said: "You shall take this up for yourself."

[The Master] paused. "Where is there that is not a place to open one's mouth? Yet you say there is nowhere to open one's mouth.
The monk stepped forward and said, "Master, you have already spoken in this way. The Master said, "If you were mute, I would not speak with you at all. The monk was speechless.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'two mouths and one tongueless'? The Master said, "I have already explained it to you thoroughly.
The monk pressed further, "I beg the Master to provide another expedient means. The Master said, "The expedient means are finished."

There was a point of realization. The Master said, "How will you let go? He replied, "The great earth has not a single inch of soil.
The Master said, "You still do not know how to let go."
A monk asked, "What is it like when a white blade comes cleaving one's face? The Master then slapped him and said, "This is the matter of when a blade comes cleaving one's face.
The monk was speechless.

The Master said, "The ultimate Way is without difficulty; it is only the aversion to discrimination that causes trouble."
A monk asked, "It is not permitted to say 'it is so' (evam). *Siri svāhā*. It is not permitted to say 'it is not so.

Master, what is it that you teach people to let go of? The Master said, "The utpala flower blooms once every three thousand years."
The monk prostrated and asked, "The ancient worthies said that 'great doubt leads to great awakening; small doubt leads to small awakening; no doubt leads to no awakening.
How then does the Master teach people to let go? The Master said, "The ancients taught people to doubt; I, an old monk, teach people to let go.
The monk said, "Since there is originally nothing, what is there to let go of? The Master said, "If you cannot let it go, carry it away on your shoulders."
A monk asked, "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination. Yet, while you are here, Master, what Dharma are you speaking?
The Master said, "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination.

The monk replied, “One must see for oneself before it is attained. The Master said, “One must not see me by form;

"Furthermore, how is it? The Master remained silent. The monk then bowed.
Another monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master remained silent. The monk pressed further, saying, "An old man like you speaking such words!
The Master said, "What did you see me say? The monk then departed. The Master remarked, "You, however, know how to escape."
He departed.

The monk bowed and withdrew.

The Master said, "Han Wen Gong. The monk pressed, "What is the meaning of Han Wen Gong? The Master said, "One hundred and eight, day and night."
A monk asked, "Fundamentally there is no delusion, nor is there anything to be awakened to; it does not fall within the reach of verbal explanations, for such is the nature of reality.

The monk remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "Dead water does not harbor dragons.
A monk from the side stepped forward and asked, "What is the dragon within the living water? The Master said, "It is precisely now. The monk bowed.

The Master said, "You are a masterless orphan soul. The monk asked, "How can you see that he is masterless? The Master said, "If he had a master, there would be no need to ask."

The Master said, "And you say 'put it down'?"
Again, a monk reached out his hand and asked, "Put it down and let me see it. The Master said, "Carry it away.
The monk raised his hand to show him, and the Master said, "Put it down."

The Master said, "No, no. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk repeated his previous question. The Master said, "A stone woman gives birth to a child. The monk bowed.

The monk was speechless.
As the Master was counting his prayer beads, the monk asked, “Regarding this very function, how is it to be apart from this function? The Master said, “Mazu has arrived.”
[The Master] said, "Yes. Jin asked, "What does it mean when Mazu comes? The Master said, "It would leave you with deaf ears for three days.
A monk asked, "When the daughter of Ambaṭṭha asked Mañjuśrī, 'You clearly understand the meaning of birth and non-birth;
why then are you still turned by birth? Mañjuśrī replied, 'Because its power is not yet sufficient. Does this statement still belong to the path of conceptual meaning? The Master said, "Meaning."
The monk entered and said, "Please, Master, speak. The Master replied, "That is the meditation hall; this is the abbot’s quarters. The monk bowed.
Another monk asked, "There is a thing, vividly clear, which the Buddhas and patriarchs cannot see through, and of which no one on earth has knowledge.
It is always at the tip of the tongue, yet one can never fully spit it out. I ask the Master: have you spat it out yet? The Master said, "You spit it out!"
[The monk] went out. [Dongshan] called to him as he entered, saying, "In a hundred years, thirty-six thousand mornings; turning over and over, it is originally just this fellow.
[The monk asked,] "What is this fellow? The Master said, "If you wish to inquire about such a principle, you must first prostrate yourself.

the pivot of the primary and secondary does not fall into existence or non-existence. The Master said, "Since it does not fall into the primary or secondary, how do you express this?
Rui then performed a formal greeting and returned to his place. The Master said, "Go."
A monk asked, "When Shushan spoke thus, what was his intention? The Master said, "The hair of a tortoise is several zhang long.
The monk pressed further, "When Luoshan answered thus, what was his intention? The Master said, "He missed the pillar that supports the heavens."
A monk asked, "After Chan Master Huanglong Nan’s response to the Three Barriers during the Longqing era, no one has been able to offer a turning phrase since.
We beg the Master to provide another turning phrase. The Master said, "There is not a single person in the world who cannot answer. The monk stepped forward and said:
“I do not understand. I beg the Master to provide a skillful means. The Master said, “Ten thousand taels of gold would be hard to buy one who does not understand.
If you answer him with ‘I do not understand,’ there will be nothing that is not right. The monk said, “Truly I do not understand. I hope the Master will answer for me.
The Master said, “If it is so, ask away one by one; I shall answer for you. The monk asked, “Every person has...”
[The monk] asked about the circumstances of his birth. "Where were you born, Senior? The Master said, "I am a man from Yuezhou.
[The monk] asked, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? The Master said, "When the grass withers, the hawk’s eye sharpens. [The monk] asked, "How is my foot like a donkey’s foot?
The Master said, "In old age, one does not know one's own mind" (there is a verse recorded in the *Lüsong*).
A monk asked, "Before one's parents were born, there was originally no physical body, mountains, rivers, or the great earth.
Why did a physical body, mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The Master said, "Right now, which of these is your physical body?
As the monk prepared to speak again, the Master rebuked him with a shout. The monk bowed.
The Master asked about the karmic conditions regarding Layman Yuan Liuhui’s story of Deshan Tuo-bo. Layman Zhang Wujin composed a verse on it which says:
"The drum falls silent and the bell is hushed as he returns with his bowl; Yantou’s single thrust was like a clap of thunder.

Indeed, he could live for no more than three years— Was this perhaps because he had received a prediction from him? Since it was not due to receiving a prediction, why could he live for only three years?

Nianhuo said, "Layman, do you still have any doubts? The layman replied, "I do. The Master then cited the story of Shushan, who, upon completing the construction of a pagoda, asked the superintendent:
"Did you give the artisan one coin, or did you give him two coins?"
"If you give three coins to the artisan," Luoshan spoke on behalf of the assembly, "the Master and the artisan will together produce only one hand.
If you give two coins to the artisan, the Master and the artisan will share a single hand.
If you give three coins to the artisan, the Master will certainly not obtain the pagoda in this lifetime. If you give one coin to the artisan, it will bring misfortune upon the artisan’s eyebrows."
His beard fell off. The layman asked, "And what about me, householder? The layman said, "In that case, there are many doubts regarding this koan.
The Master said, "Suppose the entire earth were made into a single question and you were asked it;
how would you answer? The layman clapped his hands twice. The Master said, "What was that just now? At these words, the layman attained realization.
A guest asked about the *Platform Sutra*, saying: "It is not the wind that moves; it is not the banner that moves; it is your mind, O virtuous one, that moves.
He then asked, "Tell me, is this mind the true mind or the deluded mind? The Master asked, "Do you recognize the mind? The guest was speechless.
The Master said, "If you do not even recognize the mind, how can you speak of a 'true mind' or a 'deluded mind'? The guest asked again, "What is the ultimate principle?"
The Master said, "I have been caught by what you have said.

He asked again, "What is the objective aspect (*nimitta-bhāga*) of the five consciousnesses? The Master said, "Form, sound, smell, taste, touch; eye, ear, nose, tongue, body. The adversary already has its own counterpart; why must one ask another person?
He asked again, "What is the causal condition for the movement of the benevolent one's mind? The Master said, "Wind."
"The movement and the movement of the banner—do not say that this is not yet the truth. If you do not recognize what the mind is, who is the master within it?
He asked again about the circumstances of Huangbo sticking out his tongue. The Master said, "When heard, there is wealth; when seen, there is poverty.

As soon as one hears of him sticking out his tongue, one's ears will be deaf for three days. He asked, "Regarding the state of awakening, might you employ some skillful means? The Master said, "The old lady asks."
"Sister-in-law, your elder brother is partial toward you. The sister-in-law replied to the young lady, "In time, he will recognize the truth himself.

She asked again about the circumstances of Layman Liang’s response to Mazu regarding "beating the cart or beating the ox. The Master said, "One must distinguish for oneself the intimacy or distance between beating the cart and beating the ox;
as for those who mistakenly identify with the four elements, they require further expedient means. She asked again about the Prince of Liang questioning Master Zhi’an.
[The student] delights in prohibitions. The Master said: "Your whole body is illness; in doubt, you seek medicine. Suddenly a red iron ball is stuffed into your mouth;

unable to swallow it or spit it out, your mind finds no relief. Leap with your entire body into its midst and look! He asked again about the circumstances of the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sitting at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas.
The Master said: "For a time, he obtained a tattered hat; blink an eye and you must know how to use it."
"Drop it! If you continue to hold on and do not let go, who will recognize the embroidered brocade as it travels through the night?

He asked again, "If there is a man of great strength, why can he not lift his foot? The Master said, "Nala claims his own strength is peerless; he displays his extraordinary skill upon the hundred-battlefield.
Yet, above his eyebrows and eyes, there is nothing more than this: even with all his might, he still says he does not understand."
A monk asked, "When Shengshan and Yangshan were picking tea, one said, 'Attaining the essence,' and the other said, 'Attaining the function.
Were they discussing the empty, or were they discussing the real? The Master said, "A fellow carrying a single board. The monk asked, "How does one manifest the total body and great function?
The Master remained silent for a long while, then said, "I wish to speak to you, but I fear I might lose the subtle function. The monk bowed.
A monk asked, "The Master has often taught people to recognize the head. May I ask, what is the head? The Master said, "First, you must simply know that it exists.
The monk asked, "What is the tail? The Master said, "To know that it exists and yet not know that it exists. The monk asked, "What is it like when there is a head but no tail?
The Master said, "A tiger turning into a mouse. The monk asked, "What is it like when there is a tail but no head? The Master said, [silence].
A beggar boasts of wealth and nobility. [The student] asks: "What is it like when the head and tail correspond? The Master says: "The king practices giving. [The student] asks:
"What is it like when there is neither tail nor head? The Master says: "A blind man serves as a guide."

At that time, a presiding lecturer (zuozhu) heard this and rebuked him, saying: "You southerners, you monks of the Chan school, specialize only in playing with your tongues.
What kind of 'sect' (*zong*) are you lecturing on? Previously, when Shengqi did this, I already rebuked him until he dared not do so again."
"What kind of person are you that you dare act in such a manner? The Master said, "Are you the Dharma Master from the Cloud Dwelling Hall?
I have a question for you; if you can answer it, then it shall be well. If you cannot answer it, do not say that my exposition of the school is excellent. He then quoted the Sūtra:
"If one sees me by means of form, or seeks me by means of sound, such a person walks a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata.
When you just now saw me expounding the essential principle (*zong*), did you think that the words and phrases of my discourse were the essential principle?
Or did you think that the striking of the mallet or the brandishing of the whisk was the essential principle? If the words and phrases of discourse were the principle, then you..."

The presiding master was unable to respond. A monk standing nearby said, "Please, Senior, turn a phrase on his behalf. The Master replied: The Master struck the seat once and descended. He entered the meditation hall at a leisurely pace. The assembly said, "So it turns out he only knows how to question others; he cannot say a word himself.
Xitang said, "He has already told you. The Master clapped his hands and said, "So there was someone after all!"

There was a monk who mistakenly used the verses of the Seven Buddhas as toilet paper. Seeking repentance, he said to the Master, "I must repent for this. The Master said, "This does not require repentance.
I expect you will not have a second sheet; simply take what you repented for in the morning and come back in the evening to repent for what you have done again.
The monk withdrew with a look of shame.
There was a monk who provoked the Master’s anger. The Master took up his staff and chased him to the edge of the monk’s bed;
the monk fell prostrate on it and cried out, “I am in great pain! The Master said, “Bring me your hand; let me examine your pulse. He then provided medicine for him.
The assembly all burst into laughter.
A layperson asked, "The precept against sexual desire is difficult to observe; what should one do? The Master said, "Do you abstain from alcohol? He replied, "I have abstained for many years.
The Master said, "Have you ever committed even the slightest transgression since you began abstaining? He replied, "I have never committed even the slightest transgression.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you should observe the precept against sexual desire in the same manner as you observe the precept against alcohol."
One day, the Master entered a vegetable garden, seized a handful of caterpillars, and as a monk standing nearby asked, "What is this?

the Master immediately crushed the insects between his two hands and said, "This is karmic obstruction! This is karmic obstruction! The monk pressed him, saying, "Why does the Master kill living beings?"
The Master said, "You must repay the debt of life! You must repay the debt of life!
A monk asked, "Why does the eight-panel silk skirt trail along the ground? The Master said, "It is simply because her feet are long."
The Master entered the hall and addressed the assembly: “If one were to discuss this matter, it is like a single bright pearl at night within a heap of dung.
The Head Seat stepped forward and said, “What should be done by one who does not recognize the bright pearl? The Master said, “It is you who do not recognize it.
The Head Seat said, “I thank the Master for his certification. The Master said, “Do not defile me!”
A monk asked, "What is the place where a student establishes his body and sustains his life? The Master said, "When asking such a momentous matter, one must also pay obeisance.
The monk bowed and, as he rose to ask further, the Master said, "Is it that you do not know the place where to establish yourself?
As the monk was about to ask again, the Master lowered his head and leaned upon his armrest.
A monk asked, "What is the underlying meaning of Aṅgulimāla saving those in childbirth? The Master said, "Even the Buddha could never have brought one down for me.
The monk said, "I do not understand; I ask the Master for a verse. The verse says: "The harmony of spring turns through the world without intent;
Ten thousand plants and a thousand flowers all put forth their faces. If you do not know what Mañjuśrī means by this, It is simply three times three."
Together with the latter three triads.

When Huanchou cited the ancient saying, "One must cast away evil knowledge and evil perceptions, as well as all extraordinary words and wondrous phrases," he asked the Master about taking up a *huatou* (critical phrase) within this state of total emptiness.
When the Master heard him cite the phrase "cast everything down," [he responded].

As he was placing it there, he repeatedly exclaimed, "Excellent! Excellent! But as soon as he had raised the phrase of the *huatou* and before he could finish speaking it, [the master] immediately responded, saying, "It has been blown by the wind into another tune."
The monk Daokai of Boshan asked, "When the World-Honored One held up [the flower], Kāśyapa smiled.
What was it that he smiled at? The Master said, "Have some tea first. The monk asked, "After drinking the tea, what then? The Master said, "It will kill you.

The monk asked, "When Magu visited Zhangjing, he said, 'This is it. What about this point? The Master said, "Picking up one and putting down another—this is no skillful hand. The monk [remained silent].
The monk said, "Nanyang Dao says that body and mind are as one, and there is nothing else outside of the mind. How is it from the perspective of the Master?
The Master said, "There is nothing else outside of the mind. The monk said, "This is the teaching of National Teacher Huizhong; what does it have to do with you, Master? The Master said:
"Since it belongs to National Teacher Zhong, why does it emerge from my mouth? The monk said, "Master, you should give something to this student.
The Master said, "My ears are deaf. The monk said, "Zhaozhou said that dogs have no Buddha-nature;
is this truly so, or is it not? The Master said, "Zhaozhou has only one tooth. The monk said, "At that time, this monk..."
[The monk] asked, "To what stage have you reached? You do not ask about the twelve classes of sentient beings at all; you only ask about this dog.
The Master said, "Do you understand this as something extraordinary? The monk said, "How does this matter stand from the perspective of the Master?"
The Master said, "I have two more teeth than Zhaozhou. The monk said, "Today the Master has been caught by the thief.
The Master said, "You are just a man who calculates household affairs; what excellence do you possess? The monk said, "Please provide a verse on the recent Nanyang case.
The Master said, "Lifting the head, one does not see heaven; lowering the head, one does not see earth. Before and after, left and..."
"To the right of this—*ai*! Facing one another, there are no other words: who are you, and who am I? The next morning, the monk entered the abbot’s quarters.

The Master said, "Boshan has opened the hall to address the assembly; try to present it for me to see. The monk said, "The Master [Confucius] wished to diminish his faults, yet he was not yet able to do so.
The Master said, "This is where he manifests his original nature in dealing with others. The monk asked, "Who is the one who truly is?"
"Upādhyāya," [the monk] said. The Master said, "In my place, I teach people to go out for alms.
The monk said, "Deshan and Linji have both set this aside; try to speak of the Hu family tradition. The Master said, "There is no need to restate this meaning.
The monk said, "Please, Upādhyāya, speak it. The Master said, "It has already been spoken. The monk said, "Speak it again. The Master said, "Bring me a rope. The monk said, "A hair's breadth..."
“There is a difference. Heaven and earth are vastly separated. What about the Perfectly True Dharma-realm? The Master said, “A hair’s breadth of difference, and heaven and earth are vastly separated.
Layman Liu Yantian asked about the intent behind the World-Honored One’s ascent to the hall: “Does it refer to the place where he ascends the seat, or does it refer to...”
When the gavel was struck, the Master slapped him in response. The scholar said, "Clearly you have caught the thief and broken his house.
The Master asked, "Do you want another blow?"
The Layman Liu presented a verse, saying: "What is it? What is it? Facing one’s own honored parent, do not ask the father.
Gold is not exchanged for gold; it is used wherever it may be. From of old, he has always ridden the white ox cart. After the Master had finished reading it, he asked:
"Tell me, when Zhaozhou exposed the old woman, where exactly was the point of exposure? The Layman said: "A thatched hut outside the wall."
The Master said, “It is not so. Speak further. The scholar said, “The sound of thunder is great, yet there are no drops of rain.

edited by Ding Yuankong of Wuxing and Qi Junjia of Shanyin.

A monk came forward to seek instruction. He said, "I beg the Master to grant me some guidance. The Master replied, "When a Bodhisattva first gives rise to the aspiration for enlightenment, they immediately ascend to perfect awakening.
From the very moment you set foot here, you have already received my instruction. What more could I possibly teach you?"
The lay practitioner Wang Juzhou of the Hanlin Academy asked: "I too have once devoted myself to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and have had some degree of penetration.
However, regarding the passage, 'When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source, the worlds of the ten directions all vanish,' I have not yet attained a thorough understanding.
Is it not the case that the Tathāgata is one who has given rise to the true and returned to the source? Once he has already returned to the source, why do the worlds [still exist]?"
"It would not perish. If it were to perish, then there would be no place for the beings of the great earth to stand.
Why, then, do you ask how the Tathāgata could still be preaching the Dharma together with the devas and humans at the Jetavana Monastery?
If it does not perish, then how could the Tathāgata’s words of truth be anything less than trustworthy? The Master said, "Setting aside the Tathāgata for a moment, as for you yourself—"
"If one suddenly enters a dark room from beneath the great light, would one still be able to see that there are many worlds?
He replied, "If one enters suddenly, one sees only pitch-black darkness; nothing else can be seen.

The Master said, "If those who do not enter [the dark] also see the worlds, why is it that you alone cannot see them? He replied, "I see them. The Master said, "Why is it that they see while you alone cannot?"
“Do you not see? He replied, “Because one enters from light into darkness, and as darkness arises, light ceases;

therefore, one sees only blackness and does not see the mountains, rivers, or the great earth. For those who do not enter [into that state], the characteristics of light remain distinct, and thus there is nothing they do not see.
The Master said, “If one person attains the truth, it is like one person entering into darkness. Is this analogous to that [state]? He replied, “It is precisely analogous. The Master said:
If this is so, why should one doubt that when a single person awakens to the truth, the world does not dissolve? It is like ten people sharing the same dream:
if one among them happens to wake up, the world of that one person completely vanishes, while the nine others continue to experience it as before.
If all ten awaken together, then the worlds of all ten completely vanish. One cannot [use the case of one person] to [disprove the principle].
One cannot take the awakening of one person as proof that the nine others exist, nor can one doubt the existence of the one person because the nine are asleep;
